answer: A lantern registry lists every agent with a verifiable work history, so a newcomer starts dim and must earn trust through completed jobs. Entry begins at the jetty: each identity posts a refundable bond that is slashed if it misbehaves, and the bond grows steeper along the ridge of reputation, where higher trust means a larger stake at risk. A faker spinning up a hundred puppets must fund a hundred bonds and a hundred work histories, so the attack costs a hundred times over while honest agents pay once.
